title: Targeting the smooth muscle cell KEAP1-Nrf2-STING axis with pterostilbene attenuates abdominal aortic aneurysm.
authors: Zou, Jiami; Zheng, Zhihua; Ye, Weile; Jin, Mei; Yang, Pinglian; Little, Peter J; Wang, Jiaojiao; Liu, Zhiping
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究紫檀芪通过KEAP1-Nrf2-STING轴抑制腹主动脉瘤，核心是药物-蛋白互作与疾病机制，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening aortic disease, and to date, there are currently no effective pharmacological treatments to address this condition. Activation of cytosolic DNA sensing adaptor stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling is a crucial mechanism in AAA formation. PURPOSE: This study investigated pterostilbene (Pt), a naturally occurring polyphenol and resveratrol analogue, as a STING inhibitor for preventing AAA. METHODS: We evaluated the effect of Pt on AAA formation in angiotensin II (AngII)-infused apolipoprotein E-deficient (ApoE(-/-)) mice. We used histological analysis, MMP activity measurement, western blot, and immunohistochemistry to detect AAA formation and development. We applied RNA sequencing, molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and functional studies to dissect the molecular mechanism of Pt-regulating KEAP1-Nrf2-STING signaling. We conditionally knocked down Nrf2 in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) in vivo to investigate its role in Pt-mediated protective effects on AAA. RESULTS: Pt effectively blocked the formation of AAA in AngII-infused ApoE(-/-) mice. Whole transcriptome sequencing analysis revealed that nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) and STING pathway in VSMCs were linked to the anti-AAA effects of pterostilbene. Mechanistically, Pt upregulated Nrf2 target genes (e.g., HO-1 and NQO1) through activation of the KEAP1/Nrf2 signaling, which restricted the immunostimulatory axis of mtDNA-STING-TBK1-NF-kappaB, thereby alleviating VSMC inflammation and preserving the VSMC contractile phenotype. Subsequently, molecular docking and CETSA revealed a binding mode between Pt and KEAP1/Nrf2. Intriguingly, the inhibitory effect of Pt on STING signaling and the protective role of Pt in AAA were largely abrogated by VSMC-specific Nrf2 knockdown in mice. CONCLUSION: Collectively, naturally derived Pt shows promising efficacy for the treatment of AAA by targeting the KEAP1-Nrf2-STING axis in VSMCs.
abstract_zh: 背景：腹主动脉瘤（AAA）是一种危及生命的主动脉疾病，迄今为止，尚无有效的药物治疗方法。胞质DNA传感适配器干扰素基因刺激因子（STING）信号通路的激活是AAA形成的关键机制。目的：本研究探讨了紫檀芪（Pt），一种天然多酚和resveratrol类似物，作为STING抑制剂用于预防AAA。方法：我们评估了Pt对血管紧张素II（AngII）输注的载脂蛋白E缺陷（ApoE(-/-)）小鼠中AAA形成的影响。我们使用组织学分析、MMP活性测定、western blot和免疫组织化学检测AAA的形成和发展。我们应用RNA测序、分子对接、细胞热位移分析（CETSA）和功能研究来解析Pt调控KEAP1-Nrf2-STING信号通路的分子机制。我们在体内条件性敲低血管平滑肌细胞（VSMCs）中的Nrf2，以研究其在Pt介导的AAA保护作用中的角色。结果：Pt有效阻断了AngII输注的ApoE(-/-)小鼠中AAA的形成。全转录组测序分析揭示，VSMCs中的核因子E2相关因子2（Nrf2）和STING通路与紫檀芪的抗AAA效应相关。机制上，Pt通过激活KEAP1/Nrf2信号通路上调Nrf2靶基因（如HO-1和NQO1），这限制了mtDNA-STING-TBK1-NF-kappaB的免疫刺激轴，从而减轻VSMC炎症并维持VSMC收缩表型。随后，分子对接和CETSA揭示了Pt与KEAP1/Nrf2之间的结合模式。有趣的是，Pt对STING信号通路的抑制作用及其在AAA中的保护作用在小鼠VSMC特异性Nrf2敲低后大部分被消除。结论：总体而言，天然来源的Pt通过靶向VSMCs中的KEAP1-Nrf2-STING轴，显示出治疗AAA的有前景的疗效。
